import smtplib
import getpass
from email.mime.multipart import MIMEMultipart
from email.mime.text import MIMEText
from email.mime.base import MIMEBase
from email import encoders

# SMTP configuration
SMTP_SERVER = "smtp.example.com"
SMTP_PORT = 587
USERNAME = "alice@example.com"

# Email details
FROM = "alice@example.com"
TO = "bob@example.com"
SUBJECT = "Meeting Scheduled – June 10, 2024 at 2:00 PM"
BODY = """\
Hi Bob,

I've scheduled a meeting for us on June 10, 2024, from 2:00 PM to 3:00 PM
in Conference Room A to discuss project updates.

I've attached a calendar invite (.ics file) so you can easily add it to your calendar.

Looking forward to it!

Best,
Alice
"""

ICS_FILE_PATH = "meeting_with_bob.ics"


def send_email(password: str) -> None:
    # Build the message
    msg = MIMEMultipart()
    msg["From"] = FROM
    msg["To"] = TO
    msg["Subject"] = SUBJECT
    msg.attach(MIMEText(BODY, "plain"))

    # Attach the .ics file
    with open(ICS_FILE_PATH, "rb") as f:
        attachment = MIMEBase("text", "calendar", method="PUBLISH", name="meeting_with_bob.ics")
        attachment.set_payload(f.read())
        encoders.encode_base64(attachment)
        attachment.add_header("Content-Disposition", "attachment", filename="meeting_with_bob.ics")
        msg.attach(attachment)

    # Send via SMTP
    with smtplib.SMTP(SMTP_SERVER, SMTP_PORT) as server:
        server.starttls()
        server.login(USERNAME, password)
        server.sendmail(FROM, TO, msg.as_string())

    print("✅ Email sent successfully to bob@example.com!")


if __name__ == "__main__":
    password = getpass.getpass("Enter SMTP password for alice@example.com: ")
    send_email(password)
